meta: Hand-written previews for HIGH-confidence picks only. Every factual claim is traceable to the official source linked on the match row; the validator enforces >=30 words each.

DAR-02.selection_label: Niels Zonneveld to win the match (Win Match 2-way)
DAR-02.text: Niels Zonneveld arrives in Dortmund with real momentum behind him. The PDC confirmed he starts the European Championship as fourth seed after winning the final European Tour event of the season, and that seeding earns him a first-round tie with Cameron Menzies, the 29th seed in a 32-man field drawn from the European Tour Order of Merit. Over a short best-of-11-legs format there is always room for one hot spell to flip a match, but a 25-place seeding gap plus title-winning form in his most recent event makes Zonneveld the clear call. The selection is Niels Zonneveld to win the match, and six of the seven OLBG tipsters on this market were thinking exactly the same way.

DAR-13.selection_label: Luke Littler to win the match (Win Match 2-way)
DAR-13.text: Everything about this tie screams mis-match, starting with how the market has framed it: OLBG's most-backed angle is William O'Connor getting a 3.5-leg head start, which tells you even his supporters need a cushion. Luke Littler is the reigning World Champion and, as the PDC noted when confirming this draw, he won two of the three European Tour events he entered this year — the very circuit whose Order of Merit decides who qualifies for Dortmund. O'Connor, seeded 22nd to Littler's 11th in the published draw, is a capable scorer who will have his moments, but over 11 legs he has to out-last the most relentless heavy scorer in the sport right now. The selection is Luke Littler to win the match; the only real question is the margin.

SNO-02.selection_label: Pang Junxu to win the match (Win Match)
SNO-02.text: This is exactly the kind of early-round draw the rankings exist to create. Pang Junxu, listed at 26 in the world alongside the Northern Ireland Open draw, meets Liam Davies, listed 89th, in a best-of-seven-frames second-round match at Belfast's Waterfront Hall on 21 October — a fixture confirmed on the official World Snooker Tour match centre. Short-format snooker can bite favourites, and Davies has nothing to lose, but a gap of more than sixty ranking places usually reflects a season-long difference in scoring power and match craft rather than one good week. Six of OLBG's nine tipsters sided with the favourite too. The selection is Pang Junxu to win the match and take his place in the last 16.

CRI-01.selection_label: Afghanistan to win the match (Win Match)
CRI-01.text: Sometimes the numbers and the crowd land in exactly the same place, and this one-day international is one of those times. Every one of the seven OLBG tipsters on this match — including an flagged expert — backed Afghanistan against Bangladesh, and the official ICC one-day ratings explain why: updated on 19 October, they have Afghanistan eighth on 92 points, a full ten rating points clear of Bangladesh in ninth on 82. The game falls inside the UAE tri-series window featuring these two sides and Zimbabwe between 17 and 21 October, so both teams are in 50-over rhythm rather than cold. Bangladesh are proud and awkward opponents who rarely fold, but the rating gap says Afghanistan win this more often than not. The selection is Afghanistan to win the match.
